item.title: Cottage Hill Water Works Issues Boil Notice for Neal Road Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Cottage Hill Water Works has issued a boil water notice for customers in the Neal Road area west of Forehand Lane following system upgrades performed Monday. The notice also affects residents on Ridge Way, Hillock Drive, and Knollwood Drive. According to the utility, the work required a brief interruption to water service while technicians…
item.content:encoded:
Cottage Hill Water Works has issued a boil water notice for customers in the Neal Road area west of Forehand Lane following system upgrades performed Monday. The notice also affects residents on Ridge Way, Hillock Drive, and Knollwood Drive.

According to the utility, the work required a brief interruption to water service while technicians completed the upgrades to the system. Customers in the affected areas are advised to boil water before consuming it until further notice from the water company.

Those with questions about the boil notice or how long it will remain in effect should contact Cottage Hill Water Works directly for the most current information.

item.content:encoded: A crash on Interstate 10 in Jackson County, Mississippi claimed one life and injured another early Sunday morning, according to WKRG News 5. Mississippi Highway Patrol responded to the accident around 3 a.m. on September 20. While details remain limited, the crash resulted in at least one fatality and required emergency response to the heavily traveled corridor. The incident underscores ongoing safety concerns on I-10, a major route connecting the Gulf Coast region including the Pensacola area to points east and west. No additional information about the crash's cause or the identities of those involved has been released at this time.

item.content:encoded:
Ransom Middle School celebrated the accomplishments of its top-performing students this week, welcoming new members into the National Junior Honor Society during an induction ceremony.

The NJHS recognizes outstanding middle school students across the country who demonstrate excellence in academics, leadership, and character. Members are selected based on their commitment to scholarly achievement and their contributions to their school communities.

The induction represents a milestone for the students who've met the society's rigorous standards. For many, membership in the honor society opens doors to leadership opportunities and helps build a strong academic foundation as they look ahead to high school.

item.title: I-10 Resurfacing, Road Work to Slow Escambia, Santa Rosa Drivers This Week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers heading through Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should plan for delays as construction crews tackle multiple road projects throughout the week. The Florida Department of Transportation is managing resurfacing work on Interstate 10 east of U.S. 231, along with additional maintenance activities on state roads across both counties. The I-10…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading through Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should plan for delays as construction crews tackle multiple road projects throughout the week. The Florida Department of Transportation is managing resurfacing work on Interstate 10 east of U.S. 231, along with additional maintenance activities on state roads across both counties.

The I-10 project remains one of the most significant traffic concerns for commuters traveling through the area. Drivers should expect slowdowns during daylight hours when crews are actively working, and should consider adjusting travel times or using alternate routes when possible.

Other state road projects are also underway in the region, though specific details about those additional sites weren't immediately available. FDOT recommends checking real-time traffic updates before heading out and remaining alert for work zones, reduced speed limits, and flagging operations.

Residents traveling through Escambia or Santa Rosa counties this week should allow extra time for their commutes and stay aware of changing road conditions as construction activities continue.

item.title: UWF partners with Red Sox Foundation to launch military wellness program
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida is launching a new military wellness initiative through a partnership with Home Base Florida, a program run jointly by the Red Sox Foundation and Massachusetts General Hospital. The collaboration brings Home Base's Warrior Health and Fitness program to UWF's Pensacola campus, expanding mental health and fitness…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida is launching a new military wellness initiative through a partnership with Home Base Florida, a program run jointly by the Red Sox Foundation and Massachusetts General Hospital. The collaboration brings Home Base's Warrior Health and Fitness program to UWF's Pensacola campus, expanding mental health and fitness support services available to military-connected students and veterans in the community.

Home Base Florida specializes in helping military service members, veterans, and their families address physical injuries, mental health challenges, and overall wellness through evidence-based programming. The Warrior Health and Fitness program combines clinical care with fitness and wellness activities designed specifically for the military population.

UWF, which serves a significant population of military-connected students given Pensacola's proximity to NAS Pensacola and other military installations, said the partnership strengthens its commitment to supporting veterans' transition to civilian life and higher education. The program is expected to be available to eligible students and community members through UWF's campus.

item.title: Warm start to the week with brief shower chance Monday
item.dc:creator: newsroom

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia can expect above-normal temperatures to kick off the work week, with a slight chance of afternoon showers Monday before conditions clear out.

According to the National Weather Service forecast for the area, Monday will see a 30 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms, mainly between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., with highs climbing near 91 degrees. Winds will be calm, becoming northeast around 5 mph.

Monday night, any shower activity should wrap up, with partly cloudy skies and lows around 72 degrees. Calm winds are expected to continue overnight.

If you're planning outdoor activities, the window between late morning and early afternoon might be worth watching, but the showers look to be scattered and brief. The warm, humid pattern looks to hold through at least the start of the week.

item.title: Northbound Driver Narrowly Avoids Power Lines After Sliding Off Highway 97
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The southbound vehicle drifted off the roadway while navigating a curve, crossed through a roadside ditch and into an adjacent field, authorities said. The car narrowly missed striking…
item.content:encoded: A driver in a Lincoln MKX had a close call near Walnut Hill on Sunday morning after losing control on Highway 97, according to North Escambia emergency responders. The southbound vehicle drifted off the roadway while navigating a curve, crossed through a roadside ditch and into an adjacent field, authorities said. The car narrowly missed striking high-voltage power line poles and support cables in the area. Emergency crews responded to the scene and assessed the situation. No immediate word on injuries or what caused the driver to lose control on the stretch of highway north of Pensacola.

item.title: North Escambia Seniors Get Expanded Meal Services With $62,500 Grant
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Commission has approved a $62,500 grant to restore and expand free meal programs for seniors in rural North Escambia communities. The Council on Aging of West Florida will use the funding to serve low-income older adults in Century, Cantonment, and surrounding areas who struggle with food insecurity and rising grocery expenses.…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Commission has approved a $62,500 grant to restore and expand free meal programs for seniors in rural North Escambia communities. The Council on Aging of West Florida will use the funding to serve low-income older adults in Century, Cantonment, and surrounding areas who struggle with food insecurity and rising grocery expenses.

The grant represents a significant step toward addressing nutrition challenges facing seniors outside Pensacola's urban core. Rural North Escambia residents often face barriers to accessing consistent meals, including limited transportation and fewer resources than their counterparts in more developed parts of the county.

The expanded services will help ensure that older adults in the region can access regular nutritious meals without straining already-tight household budgets. The Council on Aging administers similar programs throughout West Florida and has identified Century and Cantonment as areas where demand for senior services has grown substantially.

item.content:encoded:
Gas prices in Escambia County have climbed above the $4 per gallon mark as crude oil costs continue to push fuel expenses higher across the state and nation.

Florida saw gas prices jump 21 cents per gallon last week alone, according to reporting from North Escambia. The state average hit $4.33 per gallon on Friday, marking the highest single-day price since May 2026.

The surge reflects broader national trends driven by rising crude oil prices. Motorists in the Pensacola area should expect pump prices to remain elevated in the near term as energy markets respond to market pressures.

item.title: Florida Leaders Weigh In On November Constitutional Amendments

item.content:encoded:
State officials are increasingly taking public positions on several constitutional amendments headed for the November ballot, according to reporting from Florida's government coverage this week. The amendments, which will require voter approval, are drawing attention from elected leaders across the state as campaigns ramp up ahead of Election Day.

While details on specific amendments weren't fully available in initial reports, the pattern of officials staking out positions suggests the proposals may be controversial or significant enough to warrant public endorsement or opposition from state-level figures. Constitutional amendments in Florida require 60 percent voter approval to pass.

For Pensacola and Northwest Florida voters, these statewide ballot measures will appear alongside local races and issues in November. Residents interested in learning more about the amendments can expect increased media coverage and advocacy efforts in the coming weeks as groups on both sides of each proposal mobilize.

item.title: Austin Peay Stuns UWF With Late Rally, Wins 38-16 at Pen Air Field

Despite playing in front of home fans, UWF struggled early and couldn't recover from the deficit or overcome critical mistakes throughout the game. Austin…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's homecoming hopes took a hit Saturday night as visiting No. 14 Austin Peay pulled away in the second half to defeat the No. 17 Argonauts 38-16 at Pen Air Field.

Despite playing in front of home fans, UWF struggled early and couldn't recover from the deficit or overcome critical mistakes throughout the game. Austin Peay built momentum late in the contest to put the game firmly out of reach.

The loss marks a significant setback for the Argonauts in their Gulf South Conference schedule. UWF's next opportunity to bounce back comes with the start of their next conference matchup.

item.content:encoded:
Several Escambia County court facilities will be closed Monday, September 21 in observance of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Affected locations include the Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller offices at the M.C. Blanchard Judicial Building, the Theodore Bruno Building-Juvenile court facility, the Public Records Center, and the Billy G. Ward Courthouse in Century.

Residents and attorneys needing court services should plan accordingly and contact the courthouse for information about rescheduling any appointments or filings that may fall on the holiday.

item.title: Atmore Native Serves Aboard Nuclear Submarine USS Kentucky
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Seaman Tyanthony Dailey, a 2023 graduate of Escambia County High School, is now serving aboard the USS Kentucky, an Ohio-class ballistic-missile submarine that plays a critical role in America's nuclear deterrent strategy. Dailey, who grew up in Atmore, is among the sailors continuing the U.S. Navy's 126-year tradition of undersea operations. The…
item.content:encoded:
Seaman Tyanthony Dailey, a 2023 graduate of Escambia County High School, is now serving aboard the USS Kentucky, an Ohio-class ballistic-missile submarine that plays a critical role in America's nuclear deterrent strategy. Dailey, who grew up in Atmore, is among the sailors continuing the U.S. Navy's 126-year tradition of undersea operations.

The USS Kentucky is one of the Navy's most strategically important vessels, designed to patrol the world's oceans in relative secrecy as part of the nation's continuous at-sea deterrent. Submarine service is considered among the most demanding assignments in the military, requiring sailors to work in close quarters for extended periods while maintaining constant vigilance.

Dailey's assignment follows his recent graduation from high school in Escambia County, putting him among a select group of young service members who have chosen military careers immediately after finishing secondary education.

If you're heading outside, plan morning activities before the heat and storm potential peak in the afternoon. Stay hydrated and be ready to move indoors if thunderstorms develop.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

The closure began August 29, with crews initially targeting a Labor Day weekend reopening. Instead, commuters waited nearly three weeks before the road became passable again last Friday, September 18.…
item.content:encoded:
A section of West Roberts Road in North Escambia that shuttered in late August finally reopened Friday, though the project remains behind schedule. The closure began August 29, with crews initially targeting a Labor Day weekend reopening. Instead, commuters waited nearly three weeks before the road became passable again last Friday, September 18.

The delay marks another chapter in what locals have come to know as the West Roberts Road construction saga — a project that has tested the patience of North Escambia residents navigating the corridor. Officials haven't yet clarified whether additional closures are planned, leaving some uncertainty about what comes next for the troubled thoroughfare.

The reopening provides temporary relief for drivers in the area, though the headline in the project's history — "maybe not for long" — suggests more work remains. Residents should stay alert for future announcements about any continued construction activity on West Roberts Road.
